title: FILTER: the rows that meet a condition

screens.prompt: In B8, total the units of the orders whose status is Open, with FILTER choosing the rows and SUM adding them.

hints.syntax: =SUM(FILTER(C2:C7,B2:B7="Open")): the units are returned, the status column is tested.
hints.func-filter: FILTER applies the Open condition; without it, SUM adds every unit on the sheet.
hints.func-sum: FILTER comes back with three unit figures, and SUM is what adds them to 170.
hints.require-ref: The first argument is what comes back and the second is the test: units in C2:C7, statuses in B2:B7.
hints.value: That is the wrong set of orders. Check the status word inside the quotes and that both ranges stop at row 7.
hints.error: #N/A means no order carries that status. #VALUE! means the include test came out as text, often a lost equals sign.

reject.why: totals the shipped orders instead of the open ones
no order has that status, so FILTER has nothing to return and reports #N/A
SUMIF is the older single-condition tool this lesson replaces
adds every order, which is the total rather than the open share
counts the open orders instead of adding their units
passes the raw status text as the include argument, which is not TRUE or FALSE
returns the status words instead of the units in column C

docs.explain:
FILTER takes a block of values and a column of TRUE and FALSE tests of the same height. It returns only the rows where the test came back TRUE. The include argument B2:B7="Open" is TRUE for three orders, so FILTER hands back units of 40, 70 and 60.

Adding those three is the exercise: =SUM(FILTER(C2:C7,B2:B7="Open")) returns 170 in B8. Shipped orders come to 127 and all six orders to 297, so a formula that picks the wrong status still looks like a working formula. The status is typed inside the formula, so changing Open to Shipped re-answers the question without touching the data.

The optional third argument is the value to return when nothing matches. Leave it out and a status no order carries reports #N/A rather than an empty total.

errors.text: No order carries that status and no if_empty value was given, so there is nothing to add.
The include argument is text or the wrong height, usually a comparison that lost its equals sign or its quotes.
FILTER arrived with dynamic arrays, so a workbook opened in an older Excel cannot run it.

docs.atWork: An open ticket count that keeps up as rows arrive, and unbilled invoices asked for one client at a time.
docs.outcome: Add the rows that meet a condition without filtering the sheet first.

seo.title: FILTER: the rows that meet a condition
seo.description: FILTER keeps only rows where the test is TRUE, and SUM turns the spill into a total. The third argument replaces the #N/A when nothing matches.
